content.text:
I've set up the project in `/work`. The macOS-specific parts haven't been run yet, though: this machine is Linux, so the file-watching test was skipped and the native module wasn't installed.

**Approach:** it uses [`fsevents`](https://github.com/fsevents/fsevents) (v2.3.3), the Node binding to Apple's built-in file-change notification system, FSEvents. It watches whole folder trees and reports exactly what changed (created, modified, deleted or moved; file, folder or symlink), which Node's built-in `fs.watch` doesn't give you. The popular watcher library chokidar uses the same module under the hood.

**Files:**
- **`package.json`** – ES modules, Node 18 or later, a `mac-fswatch` command, and `fsevents` listed as optional. npm skips optional packages that don't support the platform, so `npm install` still works on Linux machines (other developers, CI).
- **`src/index.js`** – `watch(path, onEvent)` returns an async function that stops watching. `loadFsevents()` stops with a clear error if it's not on macOS or the native module is missing.
- **`bin/mac-fswatch.js`** – a command-line tool, `npx mac-fswatch [dir]`, that prints one JSON line per change and stops cleanly on Ctrl+C.
- **`test/index.test.js`** – uses Node's built-in test runner. It has a test that creates a file and checks the event (macOS only) and a test that checks the non-macOS error.
- **`README.md`** and **`.gitignore`**.

**Checked so far:** `npm install` works, and `npm test` passes the platform-error test with the macOS test skipped. Running the command on Linux exits with a clear "only available on macOS" message.

**Decision for you:** I first restricted the whole package to macOS, but that made `npm install` fail on this Linux machine, so I removed it. The code checks the platform when it runs instead. If you'd rather block installs on other systems outright, add `"os": ["darwin"]` back to `package.json`.

**Next step:** on a Mac, run `npm install && npm test` to build the native module and run the file-watching test.

Nothing is committed yet; all the files are untracked.
